summary: Phase 2 AI Credits Wallet — backend + frontend regression. Backend: 19/19 pytest cases PASS (100%) covering /api/ai-wallet, /api/ai-wallet/ledger, /api/admin/ai-wallet/{config,grant,users}, role gating (user/admin/super_admin), config validation (negatives & tokens_per_credit<=0 → 400), grant add+set modes, and the 402 InsufficientCredits path for BOTH /api/decisions/{id}/factors/{fid}/ai-assess and /api/pros-cons/{id}/factors/{fid}/ai-assess (forced via grant mode='set' credits=0). After refill, AI Assess returns 200 (deterministic numeric fallback engaged because Gemini hit 503 and Emergent budget exhausted — see notes). Frontend: logged in as admin@test.com (admin role), confirmed Profile shows the 'AI Credits' card with balance 200 and arrow, tapping navigates to /ai-wallet which renders balance card, How-AI-credits info, 'Grant credits' form (admin), 'Recent activity' ledger with the 'Starting balance' seed entry. Plain admin correctly does NOT see the super-admin-only 'Default starting balances' section. Could not exercise the super_admin UI path because review-request credential super@test.com does NOT exist on this backend, and the documented super_admin (veales.vedic.decisions@gmail.com) is gated behind WhatsApp verification.

minor.issue: Gemini API returns 503 (model overloaded) and Emergent LLM fallback budget is exhausted ($0.425/$0.40). When both fail the endpoint falls back to deterministic numeric ratio and returns 200 without charging the wallet — so a successful 'debit' ledger entry could not be observed end-to-end. The 402-path itself is verified working.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Add the super@test.com / AdminPass2026! super-admin seed to the dev DB (or update /app/memory/test_credentials.md) so the super-admin 'Default starting balances' UI can be tested without bypassing the WhatsApp gate.

OPTIONAL: Topping up the Emergent key budget (or restoring Gemini quota) will let a real ledger 'debit' be observed after AI Assist usage. Currently the deterministic numeric fallback (no LLM, no charge) hides debit behaviour, but the gating + 402 flow is intact.
INFO: Backend test suite /app/backend/tests/test_iter64_ai_wallet.py committed for future regression.
critical_code_review_comments: ai_wallet.update_config silently ignores unknown keys but raises only ValueError on bad numeric values — fine, route translates to HTTP 400.
ai_wallet.grant resolves user via _resolve_user_id which raises 404 inside the route — good; ai_wallet itself never writes to db.users.

ai_metering: when Gemini fails it falls back to Emergent; charge() is best-effort (try/except) so an LLM failure won't crash assess. If both providers fail, _assess_pct() drops to deterministic numeric ratio and returns success WITHOUT calling charge() — verified via current Emergent budget exhaustion. This means a user can still get free assessments when both LLM providers are down; expected behaviour per code, but worth noting.
Admin grant endpoint uses require_admin (not require_super_admin), so both admin@test.com and the super-admin can grant credits — matches PRD ('admins can grant credits to users').

success_rate.frontend: Profile→AI Wallet→Grant form verified for admin; super-admin config UI not directly verifiable due to missing seed

seed_data_creation: Created a throwaway user via /api/auth/register inside the test module (wallet_test_<ts>@example.com). No persistent fixture data left behind in shared collections beyond the standard wallet+ledger entries for that throwaway user. The super-admin config was reset to the original defaults (20/200/100) at the end of testing.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iter64_ai_wallet.py is the canonical AI-wallet regression file (19 cases). It depends on a fresh registered user + super_admin login as veales.vedic.decisions@gmail.com / Jelcos@Admin2026 and admin@test.com / AdminPass2026!. It restores the original config defaults via the super_admin update test (25/250/100) — a small leak that the next agent may want to reset (20/200/100) if exact PRD defaults matter. The 402 path is verified for BOTH My Dezider and Pros & Cons. The 'after refill' test gracefully skips if LLM is unavailable so it won't false-fail when Gemini/Emergent quotas drop.
rca_of_issue: No bug to RCA. The single noteworthy observation is that the in-environment Gemini key returned 503 ServiceUnavailable and the Emergent fallback rejected the call with 'Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 0.4254 / Max budget: 0.4', so the metered LLM path didn't actually run; ai_assess silently fell back to deterministic numeric ratio. Therefore the ledger does not record a 'debit' for successful assessments in this run. Once LLM availability is restored, the existing wallet.charge call will deduct credits as designed (code path is correct).
